question: Using Table 2A-2, identify the characteristic background colors for temporary traffic control, incident management, and ETC-account-only signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 2A-2 (Common Uses of Sign Colors), temporary traffic control signs use an orange background (with black legend), incident management signs use orange or fluorescent pink backgrounds (with black legend), and ETC-Account Only signs use a purple background (with black legend), with the use of purple restricted per the provisions of Chapter 2F. Standards (mandatory): - "If additional temporary guide signs are used in TTC zones, they shall have a black legend and border on an orange background." - "The background color of a canopy sign for an ETC Account-Only toll plaza lane shall be purple (see Figure 2F-16)." - "Purple underlay panels for ETC pictographs or purple backgrounds for plaques and header panels shall only be used in the manner described in Paragraphs 1 through 3 of this Section to convey the requirement of a registered ETC account on signs for lanes reserved exclusively for vehicles with such an account and on directional signs to an ETC Account-Only facility from a non-toll facility or from a toll facility that accepts multiple payment forms." - "If an ETC pictograph is used on a separate plaque in a route sign assembly (see Section 2F.05) or on a header panel within a guide sign, the plaque or the header panel shall have a purple background with a white border and the ETC pictograph shall have a white border to provide contrast between the pictograph and the background of the plaque or header panel." - "Except for ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, if incorporated within the green background of a guide sign, the ETC pictograph shall be on a white rectangular or square panel set on a purple underlay panel with a white border." Visual evidence: - [Image 5] Table 2A-2 shows Temporary Traffic Control with a black legend and orange background, Incident Management with a black legend and both orange and fluorescent pink backgrounds, and ETC-Account Only with a black legend and purple background (footnote 5: "The use of purple on signs is restricted per the provisions of Chapter 2F"). - [Image 1] Figure 2F-16 illustrates the purple background of the ETC Account-Only lane canopy sign ("Toll Pass ONLY") in contrast to the green backgrounds of other toll plaza canopy signs. - [Image 3] Figure 6P-12 shows temporary traffic control signs (W20-1, W20-4, W3-3, G20-2) with black legends on orange backgrounds in a work zone application. - [Image 4] Figure 6P-14 likewise shows orange-background temporary traffic control warning signs (W20-1, W20-7, W14-3, G20-2) used at a haul road crossing. Citations: - Page 85 - Section 6I.01 Standard §3 (p.811) - Section 2F.16 Standard §2 (p.402) - Section 2F.03 Standard §2 (p.381) - Section 2F.03 Standard §3 (p.381) - Section 2F.03 Standard §4 (p.381) - Figure 2F-16 (p.402) - Figure 6P-12 (p.883) - Figure 6P-14 (p.887)
gold_answer: Temporary traffic control: orange; incident management: fluorescent pink; ETC-account-only: purple.
